column1: # @ROOT@ is substituted with the git-sandbox root at run time and @NL@ with a
# newline (a heredoc-bearing command is multi-line, and a cell cannot hold one).
# Every generic rule (guard-kit/SPEC.md §The generic ruleset) has a firing + a
# non-firing case. Columns are tab-separated; # and blank lines are ignored.
# rule 1 — cd in a compound command
# rule 2 — git -C <repo-root> when cwd is the root
# rule 4 — absolute-path read-only repo script (rewrite) vs other script (block)
# rule 5 — repo-root absolute prefix (non-script) steered; foreign path untouched.
#          The rule declares 'sq dq hd', so a path merely *named* — quoted either
#          way, or sitting in a heredoc body — is not the executable command.
# rule 6 — shell expansion / assignment; single-quoted $ stays literal.
#          'sq' only: a double-quoted "$x" expands, and so does an
#          unquoted-delimiter heredoc body — the stated bound on the hd class.
# 'hdq': an unquoted delimiter expands, so its body stays live; a quoted one
# cannot expand, and the shell is what guarantees that — so its body is inert
# reaches rule 20's advisory, which is the correct verdict for a commit -F; the
# point is that rule 6 no longer blocks it before rule 20 is ever consulted

column2: git commit -F - <<'MSG'@NL@names a $(cmd) in the body@NL@MSG

column1: # rule 7 — unquoted brace glyph: bare {} placeholder rewritten, expansions blocked.
#          'sq dq hd': '{' is a matcher glyph, not an expansion, so a
#          double-quoted quantifier and a heredoc-body brace are both inert —
#          the corrective (spell the members) is inapplicable to either.
# rule 8 — sed reading or rewriting a file directly; a piped-into sed is a filter
# rule 9 — listing-only find steered to Glob, alone or as a ';'-batch of listings
#          (a literal banner between them is fine); action-predicate / piped /

column2: find lib -type f; find lib -type d
find lib -type f; echo ===; find lib -type d

column1: # rule 10 — bare single-file cat steered to Read, alone or as a ';'-batch of reads
#           (a literal echo/printf banner between reads is fine); multi-file, piped,
#           redirected, &&-chained, mixed, and banner-only forms are composition and pass
# rule 11 — working-tree git grep steered to Grep (a path-limited `-- <path>`
#           search is still the working tree); a revision or --cached passes
# rule 12 — self-matching process-liveness predicate: a `pgrep -f` pattern the
#           command's own text repeats can never go false, since `-f` scans the
#           waiter's own argv. A lone query, a `pgrep` without `-f`, and a pattern
#           occurring nowhere else are genuine queries and pass.

column2: bash run-smoke.sh & until ! pgrep -f run-smoke.sh; do sleep 5; done

column1: # rule 13 — bare foreground sleep steered to a condition wait. The non-firing
#           cases are the load-bearing ones: a sleep inside an `until … do … done`
#           loop *is* the sanctioned form, and a quoted mention is inert. The
#           quoted-mention row is an `allow` because rule 17 grants the append
#           outright, which still proves rule 13 inert: a block exits 2 at rule
#           13 and never reaches an auto-allow eight rules later.

column2: until grep -q DONE .tmp/smoke.log; do sleep 5; done

column1: # rule 14 — tracked-tree mutation under a live producer. The sandbox's only
#           `*.run` record names a dead pid and a non-record file sits beside
#           it, so every mutating form below declines: the rule's second
#           conjunct is a *live* record, and read-only git never reaches it at
#           all. The block arm needs a pid the test owns and lives in
# rule 15 — a backgrounded launch that records no producer is advised. The
#           shell `&` arm lives here because it *is* command text; the harness
#           flag is tool input and cannot be written in this grammar, so that
# rule 16 — `: > file` truncation auto-allowed iff every target is gitignored
# rule 17 — append-only write to gitignored targets auto-allowed. The four
#           clauses each get their refusing case, because each is what keeps the
#           grant from blessing something the redirect alone would: (a) a single
#           truncating `>` anywhere, (b) a target outside the ignore set, (c) a
#           leading command that writes somewhere other than its stdout, and the
#           single-statement half of (c) — a second statement on a line of its
#           own, which is what the heredoc residue must never be confused with.
#           Targets are relative, as rules 3 and 16's are: the runner drives the
#           guard from inside the sandbox, and an `@ROOT@`-absolute target would
#           meet rule 5's repo-root-prefix block nine rules earlier.
# the two inert targets are exempt from (a) and (b): neither is a file the
# append-only split protects, and neither is a path git check-ignore can answer
# rule 18 — read-only pipeline auto-allow; a non-roster segment falls through
# banner tolerance (rules 9 and 10's, third caller): a literal echo/printf
# segment is skipped, but at least one roster read must remain
# widened lead: a bare committed allow entry may lead, since it was reviewed —
# but only where something decorates it, so the undecorated form (rule 19's
# 'fallthrough git status' below) is still never intercepted here
# xargs is on the roster but executes rather than filters, so it is granted only
# when the command it runs is itself a roster binary. The refusing cases are the
# point of the discriminator: each is a write, and each is silently granted

column2: grep -rln foo src | xargs sed -i s/a/b/

column1: # rule 19 — decorated allowlisted bare lead with an unmatched segment blocked;
#           chaining steer, redirect steer, and the untouched non-firing cases
# rule 20 — git history-rewrite advisory: amend / commit -F / soft-reset steered;
#           a plain commit and a non-soft reset pass
# rule 21 — bare rm of a tracked path steers to 'git rm -q'; untracked,
#           gitignored, and the already-correct git rm form pass
# rule 22 — a script interpreter taking its program body from a scratch dir.
#           The firing rows are delta 3's probe table promoted from evidence into
#           fixtures: one per body source, both arms. Targets are relative, as
#           rules 3, 16 and 17's are — an `@ROOT@`-absolute one would meet rule 5
# arm (a), bash/sh: the operand form is the steer this rule inherited from a
#          consumer rule, and the stdin form is the widening the re-key buys it
# arm (b), one row per body source: operand, stdin redirect with and without the
# '-', the device-path spelling of the same redirect, and the pipe producer
# the backtick substitution — the one spelling rule 6 does not reach, which makes
# it the case whose absence would leave a silently teachable spelling. The '$(…)'
# spelling is deliberately NOT a case: rule 6 blocks it first, so a row here would
# pin another rule's verdict and go green for the wrong reason the day rule 6 changed
# falls through — the body rides in the command string, so the approver and the
# friction log both see it verbatim and there is nothing to compensate for. This
# is the boundary most likely to regress silently, so it carries the most cases
# falls through — outside the scratch scope: a tracked tool's body is reviewable
# in the repo, and the runner's own invocation takes a scratch path as an
# argument to a tracked script rather than as a body
# rule 23 — anything else falls through to the friction log
